chapter: Trumpet teachers and St. Louis heroes
title: Monday-night riverboat dances; jumping onto the boat
summary: Monday night was the night Black patrons could go on the boats. Thomas and friends jumped onto a departing boat to hear Creath, Fate Marable's band and Zutty Singleton.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: He worked for Circus Land and Fate Movable had the other gig ... I think might have been the first time I saw Zooty. And we were so anxious to hear those guys after we'd cut our lawns and did all these kind of things. Monday night was the night that's allowed for Negroes to make it.

On the boats, yes. And one night it got kind of late and the trolleys got all jammed up there, the boat was leaving. But, being active, young boys, we jumped. They pulled the line in and we jumped because we had to hear Charlie Creath.
You jumped from the landing onto the boat?
And you got on all right.

Oh, yeah. We sat there and then I went back to the bandstand ... and this-is-what-I-think- in these days, and in those days, we were taught a little more respect. You don't walk up and say, 'Hello, Charlie.'
Oh, no. You were younger, too?
Much younger. Charlie was a professional musician. I was around 16, 17.

I don't know. Charlie Creath was ageless. You couldn't tell about that guy's age, you know. But, he was a tremendous trumpet player. He had the sound of the instrument. At least a sound I liked. And, of course, we'd get on -- I think Gene Sedric was in that band. Fate Marable's band had some tremendous guys. Zooty was in that band. Charlie Creath's band ...
